mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future equity cash flows reduce the present value of expected returns, causing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS rise is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2,000 jobs is associated with stronger consumer confidence and corporate hiring plans, driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2,000 in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the identified employment surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in HOUST (industrial production) of over 2% in a quarter is interpreted as a demand shock, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as market anticipates weaker corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >2% in a quarter
failure_condition: During such HOUST drops, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) or the effect is smaller than predicted.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls for two consecutive months below its 12-month trend, it indicates a supply-side weakness that raises uncertainty and depresses equity valuations, producing a negative 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO below 12-mo trend for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified INDPRO weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 5% for three months suggests labor market tightening, which reduces inflationary pressures and supports equity valuations, yielding a positive 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: During the UNRATE decline, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising GDPC1 (GDP) above 2% annualized growth signal robust demand, which is expected to boost investor sentiment and drive a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows >2% annually for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60 days, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the GDPC1 acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) increases by more than 10% in a month, it reflects stronger consumer spending, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via optimism about future earnings.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >10% in a month
failure_condition: During the RSAFS surge, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both CPIAUCSL (CPI) and FEDFUNDS by at least 1% and 0.5% respectively over a month creates a dual pressure: higher inflation erodes real returns while lower rates boost discounting, but the combined effect is negative for 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL ↓ ≥1% AND FEDFUNDS ↓ ≥0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: During the dual decline, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or the interaction effect is not detectable in the IC.
